title: The Titanic's Secret Coal Fire (1912)
overlooked_twist: A subterranean smoldering coal fire had ignited in Bunker No. 6 ten days before the voyage. White Star Line kept it secret from passengers. The intense 1,000°C heat warped and weakened the watertight steel bulkhead, which buckled precisely where the iceberg grazed the starboard hull.
primary_sources: Testimony of Fireman John Dilley and Leading Fireman Charles Hendrickson
wikipedia_summary: The RMS Titanic sank in the North Atlantic Ocean on 15 April 1912 after striking an iceberg. Historical inquiries confirmed a persistent smoldering fire in Boiler Room 6 coal bunker had damaged the watertight bulkhead dividing bunker 6 and boiler room 5 before departure.
